raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`free_swa_out_of_window_slots` keeps `max(window, page)` tokens behind `pre_len` and floors the frontier to a page. When the window is not a whole number of pages, that can leave less than a window between the frontier and `page_floor(pre_len)`. gpt-oss runs a 127-token window (`sliding_window - 1`); at page size 64, a decode eviction at `pre_len = 63 mod 64` leaves only 64 tokens there, and with the default 128-token eviction interval and one token per step, every decode eviction lands on that residue.

`page_floor(pre_len)` is where an EAGLE request's insert ends when the next verify finishes it with one token, since a bigram key spans one token less than the request owns. The new leaf then holds 64 live SWA tokens against a 127-token window, the match after the insert rejects it, and `cache_protected_len` stays at the previous prefix. The release then frees `[cache_protected_len, owned)`, including the pages the insert just gave the tree, which the tree frees again when it evicts them. Since #41520 folded the finished insert into `checkpoint()`, gpt-oss EAGLE3 at page size 64 leaks and double-frees KV, on the default pool and on `--enable-unified-memory` alike, and on every attention backend; some runs hit an illegal memory access.

## Modifications

`mem_cache/common.py`: the retained span is now `max(window, page)` rounded up to whole pages, so the frontier stays a full window below `page_floor(pre_len)`. Page-aligned windows and page size 1 keep the old frontier; an unaligned window keeps at most one more SWA page per request.

Test (`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, CPU): `TestSWAWindowUnderBigramKey` runs a 7-token window at page size 4, the same misalignment. In `test_finish_after_decode_eviction_frees_only_the_requests_pages`, a request decodes, evicts at `pre_len` 23 and finishes at 24; before this change the full pool counts 8 tokens twice (`264 != 256`), after it every page is either free or held by the tree.

## Accuracy Tests

SM90, TP1, gpt-oss-20b with EAGLE3 on triton, page size 64, radix cache, overlap scheduler, `--mem-fraction-static 0.55`. GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy. Every server ran with the per-step pool checks and the allocator invariants on (`SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1 SGLANG_CHECK_KV_PAGE_INVARIANTS=1 SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=1`), which stop a server at the step that leaks or frees a page twice. Baseline: the default pool, run twice. Unified: `--enable-unified-memory` with lazy compaction (the default) and eager compaction (`SGLANG_DISABLE_LAZY_COMPACTION=1`), on a poisoned pool (`SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`).

| CUDA graphs | baseline / baseline repeat / unified eager / unified lazy | accept length |
|---|---|---|
| off | 0.520 / 0.544 / 0.572 / 0.524 | 1.27-1.28 |
| on | 0.521 / 0.535 / 0.530 / 0.543 | 1.27-1.28 |

Every server answered all 1314 questions with no leak, double free, invariant violation or illegal memory access. Without this change the same configuration leaked and double-freed KV on every arm, the default pool's included. gpt-oss-20b's GSM8K score moves by several points between identical runs (the two baseline runs above differ by up to 2.4).

GPU unit suite (unified-memory scope, including this test file, which is CUDA-registered): all pass except the 2 cases of `test_swa_write_back_host_full_preserves_full_and_continues`, which force the Rust TreeCore that our test image does not build.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured: the change keeps at most one more SWA page per request, and only for a window that is not a whole number of pages.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

         # up to the window boundary (the trailing floor keeps it page-aligned).
         evict_threshold = pre_len - sliding_window_size
     else:
-        # Prefix-sharing cache: keep max(window, page). The trailing floor page-aligns the
-        # frontier, and subtracting at least one page keeps it below the insert
-        # boundary (page_floor(seq_len)) so the last leaf is never all-tombstone.
-        # No extra page margin is needed.
-        evict_threshold = pre_len - max(sliding_window_size, page_size)
+        # Prefix-sharing cache: keep max(window, page) rounded up to whole pages, so
+        # a key that ends at page_floor(pre_len) still has a full window of live SWA,
+        # and the last leaf, below page_floor(seq_len), is never all-tombstone.
+        evict_threshold = pre_len - ceil_align(
+            max(sliding_window_size, page_size), page_size
+        )
     if retain_floor is not None and supports_prefix_sharing:
         # The caller owns where the floor is (see BasePrefixCache.swa_retain_floor);
         # this only promises not to free past it. Without prefix sharing a retained

@@ -11136,6 +11136,54 @@ def test_match_after_insert_reaches_the_new_leaf(self):
         cache.unlock(req.lock)
         cache.sanity_check()
 
+    def test_finish_after_decode_eviction_frees_only_the_requests_pages(self):
+        # Decode evicts at pre_len = seq_len - 1. When the last verify then commits
+        # one token, the finished insert ends at page_floor(pre_len): the frontier
+        # must sit a full window below it although the window is not page-aligned.
+        cache, allocator, req_to_token_pool = build_fixture(self.cfg)
+        page_size = self.cfg.page_size
+        full_total = allocator.full_available_size()
+        swa_total = allocator.swa_available_size()
+        prompt_len, owned = 4 * page_size, 6 * page_size
+        tokens = list(range(1, owned + 1))
+
+        req = Req(
+            rid=0,
+            origin_input_text="",
+            origin_input_ids=array("q", tokens[:prompt_len]),
+            sampling_params=SamplingParams(
+                temperature=0, max_new_tokens=owned - prompt_len
+            ),
+        )
+        req_to_token_pool.alloc([req])
+        req.output_ids = []
+        req.full_untruncated_fill_ids = array("q", tokens[:prompt_len])
+        req.extend_end = prompt_len
+        kv_indices = self._alloc_paged(allocator, owned)
+        req_to_token_pool.write((req.kv.req_pool_idx, slice(0, owned)), kv_indices)
+        req.kv.kv_committed_len = prompt_len
+        req.kv.kv_allocated_len = owned
+        req.last_node = cache.root_node_handle()
+        req.kv.cache_protected_len = 0
+        req.lock_receipt = DecLockRefParams()
+        req.extra_key = None
+        cache.checkpoint(req, up_to=prompt_len)
+
+        req.output_ids = tokens[prompt_len:]
+        req.kv.kv_committed_len = owned
+        cache.evict_sliding_windows(req, owned - 1)
+        req.finished_reason = FINISH_LENGTH(length=len(req.output_ids))
+        release_kv_cache(req, cache, checkpoint=True)
+
+        # Each page is back in the pool or held by the tree, never both.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            allocator.full_available_size() + cache.full_evictable_size(), full_total
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            allocator.swa_available_size() + cache.swa_evictable_size(), swa_total
+        )
+        cache.sanity_check()
+
